correctness.rationale: For α=−a<0, the power-mean inequality reverses when raised to the negative power and becomes discrete convexity of h_a(k)=[∏_{j=0}^ρ(k+j)]^a. The support starts at 1, and the zero-value convention imposes no extra boundary restriction. Telescoping adjacent ratios gives the stated F_ρ(a) at center 2. It vanishes at 0, has negative derivative there, is strictly convex, and diverges to +∞, so a≥a_ρ is necessary. Writing w=g′ and f=S₂/S₁² gives f′<0 by strict Cauchy–Schwarz S₂²<S₁S₃ for ρ≥1. The sliding w-weighted mean R(x) lies strictly between f(x+1) and f(x); its derivative is strictly negative because both endpoint terms have the required signs. The continuous unit slope B_a has derivative of the sign of a−R(x), so B_a(2)≥B_a(1) forces a>R(2) and strictly increasing B_a on [2,∞). This proves all later lattice inequalities strictly, including when a=a_ρ, with equality only at center 2. For the strict bounds, h_a″ has sign a−f: f(x)>1/(ρ+1) everywhere, whereas f(x)<f(1)=b_ρ for x>1, giving strictly opposite first-triple signs at the two bounds. Increasing probability ratios give strict log-convexity and rule out all α≥0 by power-mean monotonicity. An independent high-precision check of the ρ=1 defining equation confirms the printed decimal; the all-index proof is analytic.
